ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p408/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p408/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p408/r1.claim: The preceding claim that the Torah and its reports were little compared with God's knowledge led to revelation of the verse about trees as pens; this appears in the report about what the Jews said to the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p408/r1.anchor: التوراة وما فيها من الأنباء قليل في علم الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.claim: “Noble” praises created kinds either for precious beauty or for the excellence and ordered craft of every kind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p410#2/r8.anchor: ومعنى كريم: مدحته بكرم جوهره ونفاسته وحسن منظره

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r4.claim: Believers alone succeed under God’s certain promise: all creation in the heavens, earth, and between them belongs to Him, so alleged deities should show what they created.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r4.anchor: whatever is in the heavens and the earth and in between them are creatures of God. No one else has any say in it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.claim: The account specially warns fathers who pressure sons to abandon Islam, echoing the warning in 29:8: Luqmān lovingly urged his son toward the same principles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p99/r6.anchor: There is a special warning in this for people who in those times were oppressing their sons to leave Islam

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r1.claim: Most commentators hold that the heavens are spread out like a flat plate.

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r2.speaker: جميع المهندسين
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r2.claim: All astronomers or geometricians hold that the heavens are spherical.

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.speaker: الغزالي
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.claim: Al-Ghazali sides with the sphere because sensory evidence cannot be contradicted; any relevant report may be interpreted, and scripture does not explicitly require flatness but points toward circularity at 21:33.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r3.anchor: والغزالي رحمه الله قال نحن نوافقهم في ذلك فإن لهم عليها دليلا من المحسوسات

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r4.claim: Whether spherical or flat, the heavens are created by God’s power rather than existing by necessity or nature.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r4.anchor: الواجب أن يقال بأن السموات سواء كانت مستديرة أو مصفحة فهي مخلوقة بقدرة الله لا موجودة بإيجاب وطبع

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r5.claim: On al-Razi’s preferred explanation, the heavens occupy a place within limitless space only through God’s choosing; they have no support preventing displacement and remain by God’s power.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r5.anchor: وكون السماء في بعضه دون بعض ليس إلا بقدرة مختارة

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r6.claim: Some say the heavens as a whole have no place because place is what an object rests on; they distinguish occupying a position in air from resting in a place on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم المعنى أن السموات بأسرها ومجموعها لا مكان لها

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r7.claim: One reading takes the pronoun as referring to the heavens: people see them without pillars.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r7.anchor: أنه راجع إلى السموات أي ليست هي بعمد

RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r8.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to pillars: no pillars are visible, and any invisible support would be God’s power and will.
RAZI-FULL:v25p125#3/r8.anchor: أنه راجع إلى العمد أي بغير عمد مرئية

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r2.claim: The phrase may mean that the mountains were cast down from aversion to the earth’s swaying, or so that it would not sway.

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r3.claim: Earth remains stable because of its heaviness; water and winds might otherwise displace it, and a sandy, shifting earth would not support cultivation.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r3.anchor: واعلم أن الأرض ثباتها بسبب ثقلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r4.claim: A stable earth benefits moving animals: each can travel, graze, and live in suitable places, whereas unstable ground or unsuitable habitats would cause some animals to perish.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r4.anchor: إذا كانت الأرض ساكنة والحيوانات متحركة تتحرك في المواضع التي تناسبها

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r5.claim: Rain is another divine favor whose benefit depends on stable ground: seeds must remain in place until they sprout, or crops cannot grow fully.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r5.anchor: وتمامها بسكون الأرض لأن البذر إذا لم يثبت إلى أن ينبت

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r6.claim: The shift from third-person to first-person plural is an iltifat that refreshes the listener after a long stretch of one grammatical pattern; al-Razi illustrates this with successive speakers and Bakr.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r6.anchor: أما الفصاحة فمذكورة في باب الالتفات

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r7.claim: Explicitly attributing rain to God prevents people from treating it as natural: unlike animal movement, water neither chooses nor naturally rises into the sky.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r7.anchor: إذ الماء لا اختيار له فهو بإرادة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r8.claim: Rain is a conspicuous, recurrent blessing, so its direct attribution to God should prompt gratitude and bring increased mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r8.anchor: إنزال الماء نعمة ظاهرة متكررة في كل زمان

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r9.claim: Zawj means kind or species; species divide into pairs, such as trees and non-trees, then fruit-bearing and non-fruit-bearing trees.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r9.anchor: أي من كل جنس ، وكل جنس فتحته زوجان

RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r10.claim: Karim can mean productive or generous, yielding abundantly without reckoning, or honored and esteemed, the opposite of despised.
RAZI-FULL:v25p126/r10.anchor: أي ذي كرم ، لأنه يأتي كثيرا من غير حساب

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r1.claim: God created the seven heavens, as well as the Throne and Footstool.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r1.anchor: {خلق} تعالى وأوجد {السماوات} السبع وكذا الكرسي والعرش

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r2.claim: ʿAmad means supports or pillars and is the plural of ʿimad; the plural reflects the several heavens, which God made without props or columns.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r2.anchor: {بغير عمد} بفتحتين جمع عماد كأهب وأهاب وهو ما يعمد به أي : يسند

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r3.claim: Tarawnaha may be a separate clause citing what people see as proof that the heavens have no supports, or an adjective meaning there are no visible pillars, hinting that God's power supports them invisibly.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r3.anchor: للاستشهاد على ما ذكر من خلقه تعالى إياها غير معمودة

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r4.claim: God's special men are manifestations of His power and metaphysical supports of the heavens and the world's order; when they depart near Resurrection without successors, the world loses its spirit and its manifest order returns to hiddenness.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r4.anchor: ولله تعالى رجال خواص مظاهر القدرة هم العمد المعنوية للسموات والسبب الموجب لنظام العالم مطلقا

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r5.claim: Ilqa means placing or throwing something where it can be found and seen, then came to mean placing anything.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r5.anchor: الإلقاء طرح الشيء حيث تلقاه وتراه ثم صار في التعارف اسما لكل طرح

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r6.claim: Rawasi is the plural of rasiya, from rasa, to become fixed; it refers to firmly rooted mountains that also anchor the earth.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r6.anchor: والرواسي جمع راسية من رسا الشيء يرسو أي : ثبت والمراد الجبال الثوابت

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r7.claim: Describing mountains as if they were pebbles tossed by a hand belittles their size before God's greatness and portrays how every immense act is easy for Him; His command was simply Be, and it was.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r7.anchor: شبه الجبال الرواسي استحقارا لها واستقلالا لعددها وإن كانت خلقا عظيما بحصيات قبضهن قابض بيده

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r8.claim: The mountains anchored an earth that had previously been in great motion and upheaval.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r8.anchor: فأصبحت الأرض وقد أرسيت بالجبال بعد أن كانت تمور مورا أي : تضطرب

BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r9.claim: Mayd is the movement and sway of a great thing such as the earth; the ba makes the verb transitive.
BURSEVI:v7p52#2/r9.anchor: الميد اضطراب الشيء العظيم كاضطراب الأرض يقال ماد يميد ميدا وميدانا تحرك واضطرب

STUDYQURAN:31:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r1.claim: “That you see” may refer to the pillars, as translated, or to the heavens: “you see them without pillars.”
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r1.anchor: As translated, that you see refers to pillars. But it could also be understood as a reference to the heavens

STUDYQURAN:31:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r2.claim: The clause about God placing firm mountains in the earth is discussed further at 16:15.
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r2.anchor: Regarding cast into the earth firm mountains, see 16:15c.

STUDYQURAN:31:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r3.claim: Spreading beasts across the earth shows God’s Mercy in providing nourishment.
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r3.anchor: That God has spread about all manner of beast (cf. 2:164) upon the earth indicates God’s Mercy in providing nourishment (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:31:10/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r4.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r4.claim: The spread of animals across the earth also demonstrates the extent of God’s Knowledge and Power.
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r4.anchor: and the extent of His Knowledge and Power (IK)

STUDYQURAN:31:10/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r5.claim: “Beast” can mean all animals, while “every noble kind” can mean every kind of vegetation.
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r5.anchor: Beast can be understood as a reference to all animals, and every noble kind (cf. 26:7) can be understood as a reference to every form of vegetation (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:31:10/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r6.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r6.claim: Karīm also means “generous”; some take it to describe vegetation that gives abundantly without asking anything in return.
STUDYQURAN:31:10/r6.anchor: Noble translates karīm, which also means “generous” and is thus understood by some as a reference to the manner in which vegetation gives abundantly without asking anything in return (R)

BURSEVI:v7p53/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r1.claim: Mountains keep the earth from swaying; otherwise its simple parts would shift among locations and positions unless intrinsically fixed there.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r1.anchor: والمعنى كراهة أن تميل بكم فإن بساطة أجزائها تقتضي تبدل أحيازها وأوضاعها

BURSEVI:v7p53/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r2.speaker: سعدى
BURSEVI:v7p53/r2.claim: Saʿdī's poem likens the shaken earth to water and its mountains to pegs that steady it.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r2.anchor: كما قال الشيخ سعدى قدس سره :

BURSEVI:v7p53/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r3.speaker: ضحاك
BURSEVI:v7p53/r3.claim: A report in al-Muwaḍḍiḥ says God set nineteen mountains as pegs so the earth would stand, naming Qāf, Abū Qubays, Jūdī, Lebanon, and Sinai.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r3.anchor: از ضحاك نقل ميكنندكه حق سبحانه نوزده كوه را ميخ زمين كرد تابر اى بايستاد

BURSEVI:v7p53/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r4.claim: Some reports count more mountains than al-Muwaḍḍiḥ does, as Bursevī discussed under Sūrat al-Ḥijr.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r4.anchor: واعلم أن الجبال تزيد في بعض الروايات على ما فيه الموضح كما سبق في تفسير سورة الحجر

BURSEVI:v7p53/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p53/r5.claim: Some say mountains are the bones and veins of the earth.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن الجبال عظام الأرض وعروقها

BURSEVI:v7p53/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r6.speaker: أهل السلوك
BURSEVI:v7p53/r6.claim: A Sufi cosmology makes sun and moon the eyes of this manifestation and stars reflected lights in its subtle veins, known by unveiling rather than philosophy.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r6.anchor: من أهل السلوك : الشمس والقمر عينا هذا التعين والكواكب ليست مركوزة فيه

BURSEVI:v7p53/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r7.claim: God spread many kinds of animals through the earth, with abundant numbers and diverse genera.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r7.anchor: من كل نوع من أنواعها مع كثرتها واختلاف أجناسها

BURSEVI:v7p53/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r8.claim: Bathth means stirring up and scattering, like wind scattering dust or a soul disclosing its grief and evil.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r8.anchor: أصل البث إثارة الشيء وتفريقه كبث الريح التراب وبث النفس ما انطوت عليه

BURSEVI:v7p53/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r9.claim: The spreading of creatures points to God bringing into existence what was absent and making it manifest.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r9.anchor: فبث كل دابة في الأرض إشارة إلى إيجاده تعالى ما لم يكن موجودا وإظهاره إياه

BURSEVI:v7p53/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r10.claim: Dabb and dabīb mean light walking, used for animals generally and especially insects.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r10.anchor: والدب والدبيب مشي خفيف ويستعمل ذلك في الحيوان وفي الحشرات أكثر

BURSEVI:v7p53/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r11.claim: Heaven means what is above and shades one, and the water sent from it is rain from clouds.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r11.anchor: من السحاب لأن السماء في اللغة ما علاك وأظلك

BURSEVI:v7p53/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r12.claim: Rain causes plants to grow in the earth; the majestic first-person plural in both verbs highlights special care for these acts.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r12.anchor: في الأرض بسبب ذلك الماء والالتفات إلى نون العظمة في الفعلين لإبراز مزيد الاعتناء

BURSEVI:v7p53/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r13.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v7p53/r13.claim: Al-Mufradāt says anything excellent in its field is noble; here the phrase describes a useful plant species.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r13.anchor: قال في "المفردات" : وكل شيء يشرف في بابه فإنه يوصف بالكرم

BURSEVI:v7p53/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p53/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p53/r14.claim: Everything is paired through an opposite, likeness, or composition such as substance and accident or matter and form.
BURSEVI:v7p53/r14.anchor: وكل ما في العالم فإنه زوج من حيث أن له ضدا ما أو مثلا ما أو تركبا ما

TAB-FULL:v18p543/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says God created the seven heavens without pillars visible to people and refers to his earlier discussion, where he gave his preferred explanation.
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {بغير عمد ترونها} [لقمان: 10] قال: لعلها بعمد لا ترونها "

TAB-FULL:v18p543/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas suggests that the heavens may be supported by pillars people cannot see.
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {بغير عمد ترونها} [لقمان: 10] قال: لعلها بعمد لا ترونها "

TAB-FULL:v18p543/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r3.claim: Mujahid says the heavens have pillars that are invisible.
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «إنها بعمد لا ترونها»

TAB-FULL:v18p543/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r4.claim: ʿIkrima, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, says people see the heavens without visible pillars, although they do have pillars.
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، في هذا الحرف " {خلق السموات بغير عمد ترونها} قال: ترونها بغير عمد، وهي بعمد "

TAB-FULL:v18p543/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r5.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatada say the heavens have no pillars.
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {خلق السموات بغير عمد ترونها} قال: قال الحسن وقتادة: «إنها بغير عمد ترونها، ليس لها عمد»

TAB-FULL:v18p543/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explicitly says the heavens have pillars that people do not see.
TAB-FULL:v18p543/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس {بغير عمد ترونها} [لقمان: 10] قال: «لها عمد لا ترونها»

TAB-FULL:v18p544/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r1.claim: The fixed mountains on Earth prevent it from swaying or shifting to either side, allowing it to remain stable for its inhabitants.
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وألقى في الأرض رواسي} [النحل: 15] أي جبالا ". {أن تميد بكم} [النحل: 15] أثبتها بالجبال، ولولا ذلك ما أقرت عليها خلقا

TAB-FULL:v18p544/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r2.claim: Qatada says the mountains fixed the Earth; without them it would not have settled enough to support its creatures.
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وألقى في الأرض رواسي} [النحل: 15] أي جبالا ". {أن تميد بكم} [النحل: 15] أثبتها بالجبال، ولولا ذلك ما أقرت عليها خلقا

TAB-FULL:v18p544/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites an anonymous rajaz poet’s line about a colt that “أبى أن يزال ملهبا,” glossing the construction with “لا يزال” while explaining this clause.
TAB-FULL:v18p544/r3.anchor: كما قال الراجز [البحر الرجز] والمهر يأبى أن يزال ملهبا بمعنى: لا يزال.

TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r1.claim: The rain sent from heaven makes every kind of plant grow on earth; karīm describes a plant with beautiful growth.
TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {من كل زوج كريم} [الشعراء: 7] أي حسن "

TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses every noble kind as good or beautiful.
TAB-FULL:v18p544#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {من كل زوج كريم} [الشعراء: 7] أي حسن "

TABATABAI:31:7-10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:7-10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:7-10/r6.claim: Because the purchaser tries to make the Qur'an seem like false tales and treats its recitation arrogantly, the passage stresses God’s true promise, His might and wisdom, and His role as creator who may promise Paradise or punishment.
TABATABAI:31:7-10/r6.anchor: ولما كان غرض من اشترى لهو الحديث أن يلتبس الأمر على من يضله بغير علم فيحسب القرآن من الأساطير الباطلة

TABATABAI:31:10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:10/r1.claim: As discussed under 13:2, the clause may be explanatory, meaning the heavens are seen without pillars, or restrictive, meaning they lack visible pillars and may have invisible supports.
TABATABAI:31:10/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون قيدا توضيحيا، والمعنى أنكم ترونها ولا أعمدة لها

TABATABAI:31:10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:10/r2.claim: God placed lofty mountains in the earth to keep it from shaking with its inhabitants; the wording suggests a direct relation between mountains and earthquakes.
TABATABAI:31:10/r2.anchor: أي ألقى فيها جبالا شامخة لئلا تضطرب بكم وفيه إشعار بأن بين الجبال والزلازل رابطة مستقيمة

TABATABAI:31:10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:10/r3.claim: God spread across the earth every kind of animal that crawls upon it.
TABATABAI:31:10/r3.anchor: أي نشر في الأرض من كل حيوان يدب عليها

TABATABAI:31:10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:10/r4.claim: Water sent down from the sky means rain, sent from above.
TABATABAI:31:10/r4.anchor: أي وأنزلنا من جهة العلو ماء وهو المطر

TABATABAI:31:10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:10/r5.claim: The noble pairs are kinds of plants that are fine, useful, and beneficial.
TABATABAI:31:10/r5.anchor: وأنبتنا فيها شيئا من كل زوج نباتي شريف فيه منافع وله فوائد

TABATABAI:31:10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:10/r6.claim: The reference to plant pairs alludes to pairing in plants, a subject discussed under a parallel passage.
TABATABAI:31:10/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى تزوج النبات وقد تقدم الكلام فيه في نظيره

TABATABAI:31:11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:11/r1.claim: The shift from third-person reference to first-person plural signals special divine concern for the matter.
TABATABAI:31:11/r1.anchor: والالتفات فيها من الغيبة إلى التكلم مع الغير للإشارة إلى كمال العناية بأمره

TABATABAI:31:1-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:1-11/r5.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
TABATABAI:31:1-11/r5.claim: Al-Rida says the heavens are joined to earth like interwoven fingers: supporting pillars exist, but cannot be seen, reconciling the image with 13:2.
TABATABAI:31:1-11/r5.anchor: عن أبيه عن الحسين بن خالد عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال قلت له أخبرني عن قول الله تعالى

TABRISI:31:6-10/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r14.claim: God originated and brought the heavens into being.
TABRISI:31:6-10/r14.anchor: أي أنشأها واخترعها { بغير عمد ترونها } إذ لو

TABRISI:31:6-10/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r15.claim: The preferred reading is that the heavens have no supports: supports would be huge visible bodies, need supports themselves, and cause an infinite regress.
TABRISI:31:6-10/r15.anchor: إذ لو كان لها عمد لرأيتموها لأنها لو كانت تكون أجساما عظاما حتى يصح

TABRISI:31:6-10/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r16.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:31:6-10/r16.claim: Mujahid takes the phrase to mean that the heavens have pillars, but the pillars are invisible.
TABRISI:31:6-10/r16.anchor: وقيل: إن المراد { بغير عمد } مرئية والمعنى أن لها عمدا لا ترونها عن مجاهد

TABRISI:31:6-10/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r17.claim: God set firm mountains in the earth.

TABRISI:31:6-10/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r18.claim: The phrase means “lest the earth move with you”; it can be parsed as aversion or as “so that it would not move.”
TABRISI:31:6-10/r18.anchor: أن تميد بكم } أي كراهة أن تميد بكم. وقيل: لئلا تميد بكم

TABRISI:31:6-10/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r19.claim: God spread across the earth every kind of creature that moves on its surface.
TABRISI:31:6-10/r19.anchor: وبث فيها } أي فرق فيها أي في الأرض { من كل دابة } تدب على وجهها

TABRISI:31:6-10/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r20.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
TABRISI:31:6-10/r20.anchor: وأنزلنا من السماء ماء } أي غيثا ومطرا

TABRISI:31:6-10/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:6-10/r21.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:6-10/r21.claim: With the rain, God causes every noble kind of plant to grow in the earth: good vegetation with pleasant fruit.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī refers the phrase about the heavens without visible pillars to his explanation at the beginning of Sūrat al-Raʿd (13:2).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: {خلق السماوات بغير عمد ترونها} مفسر في ابتداء سورة # الرعد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p98#3/r2.claim: He refers the phrase about mountains preventing the earth from shaking to his explanation in Sūrat al-Naḥl (16:15).

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r4.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan notes a fronting in the wording and construes it as “He created the heavens, you see them without pillars.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r4.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {خلق السموات بغير عمد ترونها} [لقمان: 10] وفيها تقديم في تفسير الحسن قال: خلق السموات ترونها بغير عمد.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the heavens have pillars, but people cannot see them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة أن ابن عباس، قال: لها عمد، ولكن لا ترونها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r6.claim: The firmly set mountains stabilize the earth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r6.anchor: قال: {وألقى في الأرض رواسي} [لقمان: 10] ، يعني: الجبال أثبت بها الأرض.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r7.claim: The mountains keep the earth from shaking with its inhabitants.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r7.anchor: {أن تميد بكم} ، أي: لئلا تحرك بكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r8.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan relates that the earth initially moved, so God secured it with mountains; angels ask what is stronger than mountains, and God answers iron, fire, water, wind, and finally the human being.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r8.anchor: وحدثني أبو الأشهب، عن الحسن، قال: لما خلق الله تبارك وتعالى الأرض جعلت تميع، فلما رأت ذلك ملائكة الله، قالوا: يا ربنا هذه لا يقر لك على ظهرها خلق، فأصبح قد وقطها بالجبال، فلما رأت ملائكة الله ما قد أرسيت به الأرض، عجبوا فقالوا: يا ربنا، هل خلقت خلقا هو أشد من الجبال؟ قال: نعم الحديد، قالوا: يا ربنا هل خلقت خلقا هو أشد من الحديد؟ قال: نعم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r9.claim: In the same report, after fire, water, and wind are named as successively stronger, God says the human being is stronger than wind.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p671/r9.anchor: قالوا: يا ربنا هل خلقت خلقا هو أشد من الريح؟ قال: نعم ابن آدم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r1.claim: “Spread in it” means created in the earth.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وبث فيها} [لقمان: 10] خلق فيها، في الأرض.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r2.claim: God spread every kind of creature across the earth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r3.claim: The plants are of every color, and “noble” means good or beautiful.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p672/r3.anchor: قال: {وأنزلنا من السماء ماء فأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج} [لقمان: 10] أي: من كل لون. {كريم} ، أي: حسن.

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r1.claim: For “without pillars you see them,” Elmalılı directs readers to his commentary on 13:2.
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r1.anchor: Ra‘d Sûresi’nde ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا [13/2] âyetinin tefsirine bak.

ELMALILI:31:10-11/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r2.claim: The verse establishes God's majesty and wisdom to prepare the affirmation of oneness; the shift to first-person speech in “We sent down” and “We gave” serves this purpose.
ELMALILI:31:10-11/r2.anchor: Bu âyet, Allah teâlâ’nın izzet ü hikmetini takrir ile tevhîdi temhid ediyor. Ve onun için وَأَنزَلْنَا ile اٰتَيْنَا’da gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat buyuruluyor.

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r6.claim: God holds the heavens by His power without pillars, supports, or pegs, through His decree, will, and governance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r6.anchor: أمسك السموات بقدرته بغير عماد ، وحفظها لا إلى سناد أو مشدودة إلى أوتاد

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r7.claim: Outwardly, the firmly set mountains are mountains; inwardly, they are the spiritual substitutes and pillars who aid creation and ward off calamity from near and far.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r7.anchor: في الظاهر الجبال ، وفي الحقيقة الأبدال والأوتاد الذين هم غياث الخلق ، بهم يقيهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r8.claim: Rain from the outward heaven nourishes verdant gardens, while rain from the inward heaven nourishes the gardens of those brought near and present with God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p16#2/r8.anchor: المطر من سماء الظاهر في رياض الخضرة ؛ ومن سماء الباطن فى رياض أهل الدنو والحضرة

SAMIN-DURR:31:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:10/r1.claim: Al-Samin points to his earlier discussion in Surat al-Ra'd.

ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n7/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to note 4 on 13:2 for his discussion of the heavens' supports.

ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n8/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to note 11 on 16:15 for his explanation of the mountains that keep the earth from swaying.

ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n9/r1.claim: The shift in the divine pronoun from 'He' to 'We' signals that infinite God cannot be contained by pronouns for finite created beings; pronouns accommodate human language.
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n9/r1.anchor: the personal pronoun relating to God is suddenly changed - in this instance, from "He" to "We" - in order

ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n10/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n10/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n10/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase literally as 'thereon' and takes zawj to mean a kind, as in 26:7.
ASAD-NOTES:31:8#n10/r1.anchor: Lit., "thereon". As in 26:7, the term zawi has here the significance of "a kind".

NASHR:v2p402#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p402#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p402#2/r6.claim: All readers use fatḥa on both letters here; ʿamad is the plural of ʿimād, a support or building, glossed as a firm tall structure that keeps an elevated thing from leaning.
NASHR:v2p402#2/r6.anchor: هو بناء محكم مستطيل يمنع المرتفع أن يميل

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r1.claim: The description is evidence of God's power, wisdom, and workmanship; it lays groundwork for monotheism and refutes and rebukes idolatry.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r1.anchor: استئناف جيء به للاستشهاد بما فصل فيه على عزته عزوجل التي هي كمال القدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r2.claim: عمد is the plural of عماد, like أهب is the plural of إهاب; it means supports, and the plural reflects the multiple heavens.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r2.anchor: والعمد جمع عماد كأهب جمع أهاب وهو ما يعمد به أي يسند

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r3.claim: ترونها is an independent clause showing that if the heavens had supports, they would be visible; vision is visual, not intellectual.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r3.anchor: لأنها لو كانت لها عمد رؤيت فالجملة لا محل لها من الإعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r4.claim: Alternatively ترونها qualifies supports: the heavens have invisible pillars, interpreted as pillars of divine power; this interpretation is reported from Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r4.anchor: بغير عمد مرئية على التقييد للرمز إلى أنه تعالى عمدها بعمد لا ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r5.claim: The interpretation of unseen supports is reported from Mujahid.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r5.anchor: عمدها بعمد لا ترى وهي عمد القدرة وروى ذلك عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r6.claim: The claim that a perfect human in each age supports the heavens, which fold when humanity ends, has no basis in Quran or Sunna.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r6.anchor: ولذا إذا أنقطع الإنسان الكامل وذلك عند إنقطاع النوع الإنساني

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r7.claim: God placed lofty or firmly fixed mountains so the earth would not sway; without them surrounding waters and necessary storm winds might make it shift.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r7.anchor: أي ألقى فيها جبالا شوامخ أو ثوابت كراهة ( أن تميد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r8.claim: Some philosophers argue that on a spherical earth centered at the world's center of gravity, moving heavy objects could shift its center and move the earth, though imperceptibly because their mass is negligible.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r8.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض الفلاسفة أنه يلزم بناء على كرية الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r9.claim: Another suggestion is that without mountains, a large sea formed by flowing water and windblown sand and soil could shift the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r9.anchor: يقول : لا يبعد حركة ثقيل عليها كماء جرى من مكان إلى آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r10.claim: The verse does not limit the wisdom of mountains to preventing sway; they have innumerable other purposes.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r10.anchor: ولا دلالة في الآية على إنحصار حكمة إلقاء الرواسي فيها بسلامتها عن الميد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r11.claim: The author accepts a spherical earth, as held by al-Ghazali, and notes Ibn Abbas's report and philosophers' agreement; sense and inference support it.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p81#2/r11.anchor: كما ذهب إليه الغزالي وكذا ذهب إلى كرية السماء وجاء في رواية عن إبن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r1.claim: The verse does not prove that the heavens are immobile, as followers of Pythagoras say; other doctrines behind that view are even more plainly false.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r1.anchor: لا دلالة فيها على عدم حركتها على الإستعارة دائما كما ذهب إليه أصحاب فيثاغورس

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r2.claim: بث means bringing into existence and spreading; its root sense is stirring and dispersing, as in the images of scattered dust and dispersed moths.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r3.claim: The phrase means every kind or species of animal.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r4.claim: The water is rain and heaven means the upper direction; it may mean the canopy by figurative interpretation, but that should not be adopted without compelling evidence against observation.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r4.anchor: هو المطر والمراد بالسماء جهة العلو

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r5.claim: Plants grow because of the rain; زوج means kind and كريم means noble or highly beneficial.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r6.claim: The shift to the first-person plural in both verbs highlights care: rain and growth recur and sustain animal life and the inhabited earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p82/r6.anchor: والإلتفات إلى ضمير العظمة في الفعلين لإبراز مزيد الإعتناء بهما

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r2.claim: The explanation of the heavens made without visible pillars was given earlier in Sūrat al-Raʿd.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r3.claim: The mountains are lofty and fixed to keep the earth from swaying; its similar parts would otherwise shift positions, since none is inherently tied to one place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r3.anchor: كراهة أن تميد بكم، فإن تشابه أجزائها يقتضي تبدل أحيازها وأوضاعها

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r4.claim: God spread every kind of creature through the earth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r5.claim: A noble kind is a species abundant in benefit; the rain produces such kinds of plants.

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r6.claim: These signs demonstrate God's might, the perfection of His power, and His wisdom, the perfection of His knowledge; they prepare and establish the doctrine of divine oneness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:9-11/r6.anchor: وكأنه استدل بذلك على عزته التي هي كمال القدرة، وحكمته

BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r1.claim: The preceding titles of might and wisdom are demonstrated by the precision and firmness of God's acts in creating the heavens and earth.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r2.claim: He reads ترونها either as modifying the pillars or as a separate clause: invisible supports would show subtle wisdom, while unsupported heavens display sheer power.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r2.anchor: إن قلنا إنه صفة لعمد أو استئناف

BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r3.claim: God set mountains in the earth to keep it from swaying beneath people; the verse marvelously speaks of mountains as cast onto it although familiar mountains are below.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r3.anchor: الرواسي التي تعرفونها تكون من تحت

BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r4.claim: After making the earth stable for settlement, God dispersed every kind of animal across it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r4.anchor: فقال منبها لمظهر العظمة على أن ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r5.claim: God alone sends rain from heaven, an act no creature can bring about, and rain then supplies the means of nourishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r5.anchor: ما لا قدرة لمخلوق عليه بوجه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r6.claim: A كريم زوج is a plant kind, alike in type and beautiful, fresh, pleasing, useful, and abundant enough to sustain the animals.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p8/r6.anchor: البهجة والنضرة الجالبة للسرور والمنفعة والكثرة الحافظة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.claim: Conditionally, if Quraysh’s question about Luqman and his son occasioned the surah, these verses through 31:12 introduce the story’s knowledge, wisdom, and guidance for believers; the question thus benefited them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r5.anchor: إذا كانت هذه السورة نزلت بسبب سؤال قريش عن لقمان وابنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.claim: God’s creation is evidence against those who reject His signs: as creator of all creatures, He alone deserves divinity; assigning it to what creates nothing explains their rejection of the wise Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r1.anchor: استئناف للاستدلال على الذين دأبهم الإعراض عن آيات الله بأن الله هو خالق المخلوقات فلا يستحق غيره أن تثبت له الإلهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.claim: Treating idols as comparable to God in attributes implies denying divine wisdom, since wisdom is absent from the idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r2.anchor: فهم لما أثبتوا الإلهية لما لا يخلق شيئا كانوا كمن يزعم أن الأصنام مماثلة لله تعالى في أوصافه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.claim: The argument is ‘proof of proof’ (tadqīq): it presents a thing with its evidence and the evidence for that evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r3.anchor: ولذا فإن موقع هذه الآيات موقع دليل الدليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r4.claim: The direct address in ترونها and بكم is directed to the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r4.anchor: فالخطاب في قوله { ترونها } و { بكم } للمشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r5.claim: The phrase means ‘for fear that the earth sway beneath you’ or ‘so it does not sway you,’ as explained in the earlier parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r5.anchor: والمعنى خوف أن تميد بكم أو لئلا تميدكم كما بين هنالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r6.claim: The raised heavens without visible supports recalls the parallel in al-Ra‘d.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r6.anchor: في سورة الرعد قوله : { الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r7.claim: The mountains preventing the earth from swaying recall the parallel in al-Naḥl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r7.anchor: وتقدم في أول سورة النحل قوله وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r8.claim: The dispersal of creatures has a precedent in al-Baqara’s paired mention of creatures and wind patterns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p145/r8.anchor: في سورة البقرة قوله : { وبث فيها من كل دابة وتصريف الرياح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r1.claim: The rain wording resembles descriptions in al-Baqara and al-Ra‘d.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r1.anchor: في سورة البقرة { وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r2.claim: The shift from third-person reference to God’s first-person plural emphasizes this widely experienced blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r2.anchor: للاهتمام بهذه النعمة التي هي أكثر دورانا عند الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r3.claim: The pronoun فيها refers to the earth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r4.claim: زوج means a kind or species, as in parallel plant descriptions in Ṭā Hā and al-Ḥajj.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r4.anchor: في طه وقوله وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج في سورة الحج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r5.claim: كريم means precious or excellent within its kind, as in the Queen’s description of a precious book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r5.anchor: تقدم عند قوله تعالى إني ألقي إلي كتاب كريم في سورة النمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r6.claim: The signs also embed favors: animals supply food, milk, wool, hides and transport; plants supply grain, fruit, fodder and truffles; sea creatures benefit people too. Creation thus displays both wisdom and mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p146/r6.anchor: فإن من الدواب المبثوثة ما ينتفع به الناس من أكل لحوم أوانسها ووحوشها والانتفاع بألبانها وأصوافها وجلودها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r6.speaker: الحسن والناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and most interpreters take the pronoun in “tarawnahā” to refer to the heavens: they have no pillars and are visibly so; the word is circumstantial accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r6.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن والناس، وترونها على هذا القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r7.claim: Mujahid and Ibn ʿAbbās take the pronoun to refer to the pillars: the heavens have unseen pillars, with “tarawnahā” an adjective in the genitive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يعود الضمير على «العمد» فيكون ترونها صفة للعمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the first interpretation—that the heavens have no pillars and are visibly so—is sounder and the majority view.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r9.claim: “Tarawnahā” may alternatively be nominative by interruption, with no pillars at all.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ترونها في موضع رفع على القطع ولا عمد ثم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r10.claim: “Rawāsī” are mountains fixed firmly in the earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r10.anchor: و «الرواسي» هي الجبال التي رست أي ثبتت في الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r11.claim: “An tamīda” means “so that it not sway”; “mayd” is movement to either side and similar motion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r11.anchor: وقوله: أن تميد بمعنى لئلا تميد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r12.claim: “Zawj” here means every type; lexically it means kind or class, not the opposite of an individual.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r12.anchor: وقوله تعالى: من كل زوج أي من كل نوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r13.claim: “Karīm” may praise fine construction and ordered beauty, encompassing every kind, or praise fine substance and appearance, referring only to choice things used as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r13.anchor: وقوله تعالى: كريم يحتمل أن يريد مدحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r14.claim: “We caused to grow” encompasses all kinds of animals, plants, and minerals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p346#2/r14.anchor: وقوله: «أنبتنا» يعم جميع أنواع الحيوان وأنواع النبات والمعادن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the heavens have no columns, visible or invisible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: ليس لها عمد مرئية ولا غير مرئية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Mujahid instead say the heavens have columns people cannot see.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وعكرمة، ومجاهد: لها عمد لا ترونها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r3.claim: The mountains anchor and weigh the earth so it does not shake with its inhabitants over the water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r3.anchor: يعني: الجبال أرست الأرض وثقلتها لئلا تضطرب بأهلها على وجه الماء؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r4.claim: God scattered every kind of animal on earth; only its Creator knows the number of forms and colors.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r4.anchor: وذرأ فيها من أصناف الحيوانات مما لا يعلم عدد أشكالها وألوانها إلا الذي خلقها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r5.claim: Every noble pair is a kind of plant that is beautiful in appearance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r5.anchor: أي: من كل زوج من النبات كريم، أي: حسن المنظر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r6.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r6.claim: Al-Sha'bi says people too are plants of earth: whoever enters Paradise is noble, while whoever enters Hell is vile.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p332#2/r6.anchor: وقال الشعبي: والناس -أيضا -من نبات الأرض، فمن دخل الجنة فهو كريم،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r4.claim: The pronoun in ترونها refers to the heavens, whose visible state is evidence for their being without supports.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r4.anchor: { ترونها } الضمير فيه للسماوات ، وهو استشهاد برؤيتهم لها ، غير معمودة على قوله : { بغير عمد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r5.claim: ترونها can be an independent parenthetical clause with no syntactic position, or an adjective of عمد meaning pillars that cannot be seen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r5.anchor: لا محل لها لأنها مستأنفة . أو هي في محل الحر صفة للعمد أي : بغير عمد مرئية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r6.claim: On the adjective reading, the heavens rest on unseen pillars, namely God’s sustaining them by His power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p499/r6.anchor: يعني : أنه عمدها بعمد لا ترى ، وهي إمساكها بقدرته

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r1.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r1.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say the heavens have pillars, but the pillars are not visible.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r1.anchor: أحدهما : بعمد لا ترونها , قاله عكرمة ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the heavens were created without pillars.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنها خلقت بغير عمد , قاله الحسن وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r3.claim: The firmly set features are mountains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r3.anchor: وألقى في الأرض رواسي } أي جبالا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r4.claim: The phrase means lest the earth sway with you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r4.anchor: أن تميد بكم } أي لئلا تميد بكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r5.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r5.claim: Al-Naqqash explains the phrase as preventing the earth from moving away with you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r5.anchor: أحدهما : معناه أن لا تزول بكم , قاله النقاش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r6.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r6.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam explains it as preventing the earth from moving with you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r6.anchor: الثاني : أن لا تتحرك بكم , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r7.claim: One account says the earth rocked like a ship and was stabilized with nineteen mountains branching through it as pegs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن الأرض كانت تتكفأ مثل السفينة فأرساها الله بالجبال وأنها تسعة عشر جبلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r8.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report transmitted by Abu al-Ashhab, says the earth began to sway when created; angels feared no creature could remain upon it, then marveled when mountains anchored it, and learned that wind and then Adam's child were stronger than mountains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r8.anchor: وروى أبو الأشهب عن الحسن قال : لما خلق الله الأرض جعلت تميد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r9.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r9.claim: Al-Suddi glosses God spread creatures in the earth as created them there.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r10.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the verb as spread or extended.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r11.claim: A third gloss is that God dispersed every kind of animal; dābba is named for its motion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r11.anchor: الثالث : فرق فيها من كل دابة وهو الحيوان سمي بذلك لدبيبه والدبيب الحركة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r12.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the phrase refers to human beings as vegetation of the earth: those entering Paradise are noble and those entering the Fire are base.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r12.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم الناس هم نبات الأرض فمن دخل الجنة فهو كريم ومن دخل النار فهو لئيم , قاله الشعبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r13.claim: Another view takes the phrase as the earth's vegetation, trees, and crops, with zawj meaning a kind or species.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r13.anchor: الثاني : أن نبات الأرض أشجارها وزرعها , والزوج هو النوع .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r15.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r15.claim: Ibn Isa glosses noble as having good fruit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r15.anchor: الثاني : أنه الطيب الثمر , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r16.speaker: ابن كامل
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r16.claim: Ibn Kamil glosses noble as ripe.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r16.anchor: الثالث : أنه اليانع , قاله ابن كامل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r17.claim: Mawardi suggests a further sense: noble could mean valuable because of its high price.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p329/r17.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أن الكريم ما كثر ثمنه لنفاسة القدر .

MUQATIL:31:8-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r2.claim: Muqatil notes fronting in the phrase: the seven heavens stand without supports, and people see them standing so.
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r2.anchor: يقول: هن قائمات ليس لهن عمد

MUQATIL:31:8-11/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r3.claim: God placed mountains in the earth to keep it from shifting beneath people.

MUQATIL:31:8-11/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r4.claim: God created every kind of creature in the earth.
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r4.anchor: يقول: خلق في الأرض من كل دابة

MUQATIL:31:8-11/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:8-11/r5.claim: God sent rain from heaven and brought forth every beautiful kind of plant in the earth.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r1.claim: ʿAmad is the plural of ʿimād, a pillar or support.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r2.claim: The pronoun refers to the heavens. The phrase can stand independently as evidence that they are visibly unsupported, or modify ʿamad as 'pillars that are not seen'; the latter means God holds the heavens by His power.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r2.anchor: الضمير للسموات وهو استشهاد برؤيتهم لها غير معمودة على قوله بغير عمد كما تقول لصاحبك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r3.claim: On the reading with unseen pillars, the heavens are sustained by God's power even though their supports are not visible.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r3.anchor: يعنى أنه عمدها بعمد لا ترى وهو امساكها بقدرته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r5.claim: The mountains were placed so that the earth would not shake with you.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r6.claim: Baththa means to scatter and spread abroad.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r6.anchor: ﴿ وبث ﴾ ونشر ﴿ فيها من كل دابة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p281#4/r7.claim: Zawj means a kind or species.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r1.claim: If tarawnahā modifies ʿamad, it is genitive and allows unseen pillars to exist; if circumstantial of the heavens, it is accusative and means there are no pillars at all.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r1.anchor: تكون «ترونها» في موضع خفض على النعت ل«عمد» فيمكن أن يكون ثم عمد ولكن لا ترى. ويجوز أن تكون في موضع نصب

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r2.speaker: علي بن سليمان ومكي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r2.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān, followed by Makkī, prefers tarawnahā as a new sentence: there are no pillars; bi-ghayri ʿamad then completes the phrase.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r2.anchor: النحاس: وسمعت علي بن سليمان يقول: الأولى أن يكون مستأنفا، ولا عمد ثم قاله مكي.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r3.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier discussion of this phrase in al-Raʿd.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r3.anchor: وقد مضى في «الرعد» الكلام في هذه الآية.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r4.anchor: { وألقى في الأرض رواسي } أي جبالا ثوابت.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r5.claim: The clause is accusative, meaning aversion to the earth’s swaying; the Kūfans parse it as meaning lest it sway.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r5.anchor: { أن تميد } في موضع نصب أي كراهية أن تميد. والكوفيون يقدرونه بمعنى لئلا تميد.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains a noble pair as every beautiful color or kind.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: من كل لون حسن.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r7.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī applies the phrase to people, made from earth: those destined for Paradise are noble and those destined for Hell are base.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r7.anchor: وتأوله الشعبي على الناس لأنهم مخلوقون من الأرض قال: من كان منهم يصير إلى الجنة فهو الكريم،

QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r8.claim: Another explanation says semen is created from soil, which the author says is supported by the Qurʾān’s apparent wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:10-11/r8.anchor: وقد تأول غيره أن النطفة مخلوقة من تراب، وظاهر القرآن يدل على ذلك.
